About Real Equine Dentistry

I am a fully insured and qualified BEVA/BVDA equine dental technician and member of the British Association of Equine Dental Technicians (BAEDT), providing a professional, knowledgeable and reliable service to all equines across the South West.

I have a range of experience — from the competition horse and the happy hacker, to welfare and charity cases of all shapes, ages and sizes. My aim is to provide a pleasant and educational visit for both horse and owner.

Alongside this, I'm also a Registered Veterinary Nurse with over 16 years of clinical experience, which has given me an extensive understanding of horse behaviour. If your horse requires sedation, I'm happy to liaise with your vet to arrange a suitable plan.

Know the Signs

What to watch for between visits

Horses are stoic about mouth pain, so the signs are often subtle. Any of these are worth a call.

01

Dropping feed

Spilling grain or "quidding" — balling up and dropping hay while chewing.

02

Head tilting

Chewing awkwardly to one side, or tilting the head while eating.

03

Bit resistance

New head-shaking, leaning on the bit, or reluctance to take contact.

04

Weight loss

Slow eating or dropped condition despite a consistent diet.

05

Foul odour

Unpleasant breath or nasal discharge can point to dental disease.

06

Uneven wear

Sharp points, hooks or waves felt during a routine check.

Services

Dental care for every stage

From first-ridden youngsters to retired welfare cases — every visit is paced to the individual horse.

Routine Examinations

Full oral checks to catch sharp enamel points, hooks and early pathology before they affect condition or ridden work.

Rasping & Floating

Hand and motorised rasping to correct uneven wear and restore a comfortable, balanced bite.

Sedation Coordination

Where sedation is needed for a thorough exam, I liaise directly with your vet to plan a safe, low-stress visit.

Youngster & Bit Seating

Checks for wolf teeth and sharp points before backing, so the first bit is a comfortable introduction.

Veteran & Welfare Care

Gentle, patient dentistry for older horses and welfare cases, with condition and comfort always front of mind.

Pre-Purchase Checks

A clear, honest dental assessment as part of your vetting process, with findings explained plainly.
